before: The not-ready status information shall be indicated to the driver until the system has been successfully initialised.
after: If ACPE is not ready to intervene 6 seconds after initiation of the vehicle powertrain, the not-ready status information shall be indicated to the driver until the system has been successfully initialised.
reason: Preserve the six-second trigger when the persistence obligation is listed separately from the warning trigger.

evidence.text:
5.1.4.1. If ACPE is not ready to perform an intervention 6 seconds after the initiation of the vehicle powertrain,
information of this status shall be indicated to the driver. This information shall exist until the system has been
successfully initialised.

before: The collision speed shall not be greater than 70% of the speed the vehicle would have had in the same position and circumstances without any ACPE intervention.
after: If a collision is not prevented, the collision speed shall not be greater than 70% of the speed the vehicle would have had in the same position and circumstances without any ACPE intervention.
reason: Restore the shared collision-not-prevented condition on the separately listed 70 percent constraint.

evidence.text:
5.1.6. In the case that a collision is not prevented, the collision speed shall be no greater than 8 km/h higher than
the vehicle speed at the point where the triggering conditions specified in paragraph 5.1.2. are met.
In addition, the collision speed shall not be greater than 70% of that speed the vehicle would have had in the same
position and under the same circumstances but without any ACPE intervention.

before: The change-over mechanism principles, logic and level of redundancy, built-in back-up checking features shall be explained and the resulting limits of back-up effectiveness defined.
after: If the chosen provision selects a second back-up means to realise the vehicle control system objective, the change-over mechanism principles, logic and level of redundancy, built-in back-up checking features shall be explained and the resulting limits of back-up effectiveness defined.
reason: Backup design documentation applies when that safety architecture is selected, not unconditionally.

evidence.text:
3.4.3.2. If the chosen provision selects a second (back-up) means to realise the vehicle control system objective,
the principles of the change-over mechanism, the logic and level of redundancy and any built in back-up checking

before: the remaining section may be tested statically.
after: Under the combined static and dynamic test option, the remaining section of the headform test area, outside the region required to be tested dynamically where HIT_d < TRT, may be tested statically.
reason: Restore the missing subject and condition of an isolated sentence fragment; preserve the permission and its dynamic-test sibling.

evidence.text:
4.3. "Combined" test option:
Combined static and dynamic tests may apply, at manufacturer’s choice.
If the headform test area consists of sections where the HIT_d at the corresponding impact point is less than TRT
(HIT_d <TRT) , as in the A section in Figure 1-1, and sections where the HIT_d at the corresponding impact point
is greater than or equal to TRT (HIT_d ≥TRT, as in the B section in Figure 1-1, then all test points forward of the
corresponding WAD (HIT_d < TRT) shall be tested dynamically. The remaining section of the headform test area
may be tested statically (see Figure 1-5 below, obtained from Annex 2, Figure 2-2).

before: Replaceable light source module(s) shall bear a specific identification code comprising the starting letters "MD" followed by the approval mark without the circle, followed by additional symbols or characters.
after: Replaceable light source modules shall bear a specific identification code comprising the starting letters "MD" followed by the approval mark without the circle; additional symbols or characters shall follow if several non-identical light source modules are used.
reason: Additional identification symbols are conditional on several non-identical modules; the input made them unconditional.

evidence.text:
3.3.3.5. In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, bear the following markings.
(a) On the light source module(s):
(i) The trade name or mark of the applicant;
(ii) The specific identification code of the module; This specific identification code shall comprise the starting
letters “MD” for “MODULE” followed by the approval mark without the circle as prescribed in paragraph

3.3.2.1.1. In case several non-identical light source modules are used, followed by additional symbols or
characters; The approval mark does not have to be the same as the one on the lamp in which the module is used,
but both marks shall be from the same applicant;
(iii) The rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
(b) On the lamp:
(i) The specific identification code of the module as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.3.5. (a), (ii);
(ii) The rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.

before: Alternatively, such lamps may be tested using one light source in each lamp holder position operating at the reference/objective luminous flux, summing the measured luminous intensities for each direction.
after: Alternatively, lamps equipped with multiple replaceable UN approved light sources may be tested using one light source in each individual lamp holder position at the reference/objective luminous flux, summing the measured luminous intensities for each direction.
reason: Replace the orphaned subject such lamps with the explicit parent-clause scope.

evidence.text:
4.8.2.3. In case of lamps equipped with multiple replaceable UN approved light sources:
4.8.2.3.1. shall be operated at a voltage or electrical current setting such that the actual luminous fluxes of the
light sources do not deviate by more than 5 per cent from the average luminous flux of the light sources. The
measured luminous intensities shall be corrected proportionally for the difference between the average luminous
flux and the applicable reference/objective luminous flux.
4.8.2.3.2. alternatively, may be tested by using one light source in each of the individual lamp holder positions
operating at the reference/objective luminous flux and application of the sum of the measured luminous intensities
for each direction.
